desc: Establish correct theory: feasible ⟹ cost ≤ 3. After cost-1 and all cost-2 cases fail: 2b-failure gives maxL ≤ minR (common point in every interval), so op2(argmaxL) + op2(argminR) leaves exactly [maxL,minR] uncovered and op1(any third index) covers it. a≠b guaranteed (a=b would force containment → cost-2c). Hence after cost-1/2 fail: answer is 3 if M≥3, else -1 for M≤2 with no cost-1/2 solution.

Implement full solution: fast IO; cost-1 full-interval op1; cost-2a chain (best l==1 interval + best r==N interval, R_left ≥ L_right − 1); cost-2b disjoint holes (minR < maxL); cost-2c containment via sort (L asc, R desc) + max-R sweep; cost-3 via argmaxL/argminR/third distinct index; else -1. Output K then op_1..op_M. Code reviewed: parsing, index tracking, distinct-index handling, and all four samples traced correctly.

Stress test against brute force for small N,M: verified minimality and actual coverage, including cost-3 witnesses, duplicates (cost 2 via op1+op2 on equal intervals), touching boundaries (R+1 chaining), N=1, M=1/2 infeasible cases, and all four samples. All checks passed.
